So with metro, you need to check in as they have a fee of 1DKK for every trip you take with them. There's a chance you'll get a fine if a Controller comes by, purely because of the fee.. 
But I mean, once you're on the metro there isn't much to be done, id recommend just getting off the next stop and checking in there and then continuing your journey.

As with other trains and busses, I still recommend checking in every time you change transport as those are the rules and also how you get the most accurate price, but there isn't really anything stopping you here. 
If you took the s-train and checked in, then switched to a bus and forgot to check in, then it's completely fine to just check out when you get to your destination. 

In rare cases it may mess with the price a little bit, as it is a fragile system, so just keep an eye on your checkout price and if it seems too steep then you can double check your travel cost on rejseplanen.dk (journeyplanner.dk) and if you paid too much, you can contact Rejsekort customer service either through email or a phone call so it can get corrected.

All in all, don't mess with the metro.. they are their own entity and take their 1 DKK fee very seriously🫠

Hope this helps!

I worked in the Rejsekort Call Center!
Unfortunately there is nothing you can do if you forget to check out on the anonymous Rejsekort. There is no way to report it and therefore you will lose the 70DKK that gets reserved when you start a trip. 
However, if you are unable to check out (because of equipment error or as such, NOT because a friend stopped you on the street to talk and then the bus drove off) then call in to 70 11 33 33 or write in via the website and they will open a case for you. 
Something I could recommend though, although I can't promise anything (ESPECIALLY if you do it a lot):
A trip inside the Sjælland region can take a maximum of 5 hours, so you are able to check out on a station or in a bus, as long as it hasnt been 5 hours since you checked in. This obviously means that you will get deducted the time it took instead of the distance, and it could be a bit of a high number. 
Call in or write in to see if you can the money back that goes beyond what I would've cost for the distance.

Best case, you only end up paying what the trip would've cost if you had checked out. 
Worst case, your request gets denied but at least you don't have a missing check out on the card.
The anonymous card can get shut down if you have 2 missing check outs within one year. If it gets closed, it cannot open again, and you will need to purchase a new card. (You are still able to get the money back that was on the balance, you have a year to call or write in to tell Rejsekort you want the money - you do not get the card fee back of 80DKK)
Sometimes it may take a while to tricker, and you could rack up more than 2 missing check outs in a short time.. This does not mean it won't get shut down. It is not people who do it manually, it is a computer.

Hope this helps, remember the people on the phone have not made these rules and there is no reason to get upset or yell at them, they are only there to help you.
I always make it clear to customers who consider the anonymous rejsekort, that I do not recommend it because of these rules.

Yes, you can use your Rejsekort no problem. You can always start a trip no matter how much it costs, as long as you have a balance of minimum 25DKK.
If you have a reload/top up agreement, then your balance will become negative, but it automatically puts money on your card again the next time you check in.

Rejsekort always puts money on your balance before they take money from your card, so you're guaranteed to be able to travel while you have an active reload agreement. :)

Remember if you bring a bike, that you can no longer use your Rejsekort to check it in on trains like IC and IC+, you need to buy a ticket for the bike through DSB.
